From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@carelogic.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capture controls / derivative licensing for pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the model latency looked promising. Legal and InfoSec asked me to gather a concrete set of options around how CareLogic customer data (prompts + model responses + session state) would be handled if we move forward with a pilot. Their questions are in the attached spreadsheet but high level: 

- We need a strong guarantee that customer prompts and generated responses will not be used for model improvement or shared with other customers. A binary yes/no for whether you will use customer data to train or improve models would be ideal.
- If you do not make that guarantee, what technical controls do you provide (per-customer toggles, retention windows, explicit deletion APIs)?
- What licensing do we have to the model outputs? We need clarity on whether the vendor or customer holds any derivative IP rights, and whether the customer can request that derivative rights be revoked or restricted after the fact.
- Subprocessors: we need a full list and an onshore-in-EU option. Any transfer to US or third countries requires SCCs and an explanation of how data is isolated.

We prefer an implementation that avoids model learning entirely, but we recognize that sometimes a dedicated path is acceptable. Could you please: (a) describe the implementation options with pros/cons; (b) provide suggested contract language we can give to our counsel for a DPA amendment; and (c) confirm approximate timeline and any procurement impact for the pilot?

I attached the spreadsheet with line-by-line asks. If helpful we can set a short call with procurement/legal next week.

Thanks —
Elena Soto
Head of Data Governance
CareLogic Health

Attachment: CareLogic_DPA_Questions.xlsx

Hi Elena — great questions, thanks for the clear spreadsheet. Quick summary up-front and then detail below:

Summary options (tradeoffs in parentheses):
1) Capture-exclusion (policy-level): we commit that data from your tenant will not be used for model improvement, enforced via per-tenant capture toggles and a short retention window (operational control; minimal engineering lead time).
2) Isolation mode (architectural): dedicated inference pool + onshore KMS + no telemetry outside the pool (stronger assurance; higher cost and provisioning time).
3) Output-licensing addendum: sample amendment that clarifies customer ownership of prompt/response content and provides a mechanism for the customer to request revocation or restriction of any derivative licensing within a 30-day remediation window.

Below are the specifics you can share with counsel. Ive looped in Rishi from Legal and Dev for feasibility and ops impact. Ill also attach an operations diagram.

Technical controls (what we can do today):
- Per-tenant capture toggle: can be enabled at onboarding to exclude telemetry from logging paths used by model improvement pipelines.
- Retention: default 30-day session retention for pilot mode; can be shortened to 7 days or configured to auto-delete on policy.
- Ephemeral KV and API-level redaction: we can redact named PHI fields before storage on request (pattern-based).
- Dedicated inference pool: reserved GPUs that prevent cross-tenant transfer and prevent telemetry export; recommended for customers requiring contractual isolation.
- Attestation: we can provide a signed operational attestation and an exportable audit log showing deletion events and subprocessor interactions.

Contract language (draft bullets you can pass to counsel):
- Capture-exclusion clause: "Redwood agrees not to use, access, or otherwise process Customer Data for the purpose of training, fine-tuning, or improving any machine learning models used by Redwood, except to the extent necessary to provide the Service to the Customer."
- Derivative licensing: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data and Customer Output. Redwood is granted a limited, revocable license to process Customer Data solely to provide the Service. Upon Customer notice, Redwood will cease any derivative use and will remove Customer Data from improvement pipelines within 30 days and confirm deletion via attestation."
- Subprocessor/residency: list of subprocessors provided upon request; for EU residency we offer an onshore-backed deployment option (EU region + onshore KMS + SCCs).

Ops/Procurement notes:
- Capture-exclusion and the 30-day retention configuration are standard at onboarding and do not change list pricing.
- Dedicated isolation mode requires a Dedicated quote (approx +40% over hosted for pilot-sized pool) and ~3 week lead time to provision.

Next steps:
- Rishi: can you review the two draft bullets above and suggest precise contract language for the DPA amendment?
- Dev: can you confirm feasibility of a per-tenant attestation and the timeline to enable redaction rules?
- Elena/Tom: happy to set a 30-minute call to walk through the tradeoffs.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Rishi — quick feasibility note from engineering: 

- Per-tenant capture toggle: feasible today. We have a flag at the request-router level that prevents data from being copied into the model-improvement pipeline. We can expose this as an onboarding switch or API. Estimated dev work to make this audit-exportable and attach deletion events: 1 sprint (2 weeks) to implement attestation export + 1 week QA.
- Retention windows & auto-delete: storage already supports TTLs; we can add a per-tenant override (config + API) in ~5 business days.
- Redaction/patterns: we have PII/PHI regexes in the pipeline; can add customer-specific redaction rules but it will require a brief operational validation cycle (~1 week).
- Dedicated isolation: provisioning Dedicated for a pilot (2-3 reserved A100s equivalent) is operationally straightforward; lead time ~3 weeks for provisioning + KMS onboarding.

Risk/notes: the attestation will be an operational artifact stating that data was excluded/removed from training pipelines; it does not replace a legal covenant. For customers who want absolute cryptographic proof we can design additional logging but that is a larger effort.

Ill prepare a short ops note we can share on Monday with timelines and steps for both hosted+capture-toggle and Dedicated isolation.

— Dev
